Title: Designing and evaluating large language model-enabled clinical decision support for heart failure: a modular and risk-tiered framework
Summary: Proposes and evaluates a modular, risk-tiered framework for embedding LLMs into clinical decision support for heart failure management. The design stratifies recommendations by risk level to balance automation with clinician oversight in high-stakes cardiac care.
Outcome: clinical decision support / treatment recommendations

Title: Performance of large language models and clinical decision support in perioperative management of oral anticoagulants
Summary: Assesses baseline LLM performance on perioperative anticoagulation management decisions and finds it modest and insufficient to replace clinical judgment alone. Integrating structured clinical decision support tools alongside the LLM produced marked, clinically meaningful improvements in accuracy.
Outcome: clinical decision accuracy for anticoagulation management

Title: Guideline-Integrated Large Language Models Improve Decision Support for Acute Ear, Nose and Throat Emergencies
Summary: Examines whether LLMs can reliably apply specialty guidelines in time-sensitive ENT emergency settings. Retrieval-augmented generation grounded in clinical guidelines improved reliability, safety, and guideline alignment of the LLM's decision-support outputs.
Outcome: guideline-adherent decision support quality

Title: Augmenting clinical decision-making with large language models: evaluation across general and specialty tasks
Summary: Evaluates LLM-augmented clinical decision-making across a range of general and specialty-specific clinical tasks. Compares performance to assess where LLM assistance adds the most value versus where limitations remain.
Outcome: clinical decision-making performance across tasks

Title: Advancing Knowledge in Evaluating the Clinical Impact of Large Language Models for Clinical Text Summarization: A Narrative Review
Summary: A narrative review synthesizing evidence on how LLMs are used and evaluated for summarizing clinical text from electronic health records. Discusses methods for assessing clinical impact and highlights persistent concerns about hallucination and omission in generated summaries.
Outcome: clinical text summarization quality/impact

Title: Large Language Models for Clinical Narrative Processing: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
Summary: Reviews methods, applications, and open challenges for using LLMs to process clinical narratives, including information extraction, summarization, triage prediction, and section classification. Notes that LLMs often surpass traditional machine-learning approaches on these tasks but still face challenges around reliability.
Outcome: clinical narrative processing (extraction, summarization, triage, classification)

Title: How Good Are Patient-Facing LLMs at Survivorship Questions? A Comparative User Evaluation Across Four Chatbots
Summary: Compares four patient-facing LLM chatbots on their ability to answer cancer survivorship questions, evaluated by cancer survivors themselves. Identifies trust, accuracy, provenance, personalization, empathy, and risk-based escalation as key themes governing patients' willingness to act on chatbot responses.
Outcome: patient question-answering quality/trust

Title: Feasibility and user evaluation of HopeBot: An LLM-powered conversational chatbot for depression screening
Summary: Introduces HopeBot, an LLM-powered conversational agent that administers the PHQ-9 depression screening instrument via text or voice with real-time clarification. Reports feasibility and user evaluation results for this patient-facing screening tool.
Outcome: depression screening (PHQ-9 administration)

Title: Impact of Large Language Model-Based AI Tools on Physician-Patient Communication: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining how LLM-based AI tools affect physician-patient communication. Finds that LLM-generated responses tend to be more empathetic, detailed, and understandable, with potential positive effects on patient experience and engagement.
Outcome: physician-patient communication quality (empathy, patient experience)

Title: Evaluating Small Open LLMs for Medical Question Answering: A Practical Framework
Summary: Proposes a practical framework for evaluating small, open-weight LLMs on medical question answering, arguing that high average accuracy alone is insufficient. Emphasizes the need for models to consistently return reliable answers across varied clinical questions.
Outcome: medical question-answering accuracy/reliability

Title: Large Language Models and Adverse Event Detection Within Immunotherapy Clinical Trials
Summary: Evaluates the use of large language models to automatically detect and flag adverse events reported within immunotherapy clinical trial records. Assesses accuracy of LLM-based extraction compared to manual clinical trial safety review.
Outcome: adverse event detection in clinical trials

Title: Large Language Models in Post-Acute and Long-Term Care: Bridging Promise and Practice
Summary: Discusses opportunities and practical barriers to deploying LLMs in post-acute and long-term care settings. Reviews current applications and outlines steps needed to translate promise into routine clinical practice.
Outcome: applications and adoption in post-acute/long-term care

Title: Structured Clinical Input-Guided Large Language Model Workflow for Acute Ischemic Stroke Discharge Education: A Multicenter Feasibility Study
Summary: Tests a multicenter workflow in which structured clinical inputs guide an LLM to generate patient discharge education materials for acute ischemic stroke. Reports on feasibility and quality of the LLM-generated discharge education content.
Outcome: quality of generated discharge education materials

Title: Benchmarking agreement between large language models and published clinical trial conclusions across four artificial intelligence platforms
Summary: Compares ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok3, and Claude on their ability to interpret numerical and statistical results from 20 landmark NEJM randomized controlled trials and reach conclusions matching the published findings. ChatGPT showed the highest concordance (100%), followed by Gemini, Grok3, and Claude, though possible training-data leakage limits interpretation.
Outcome: agreement/concordance with published clinical trial conclusions

Title: LLM-in-the-Loop execution of clinical quality language
Summary: Proposes and evaluates a workflow that keeps a large language model in the loop during execution of clinical quality language for automated quality-measure computation. Examines how LLM assistance affects accuracy and efficiency of clinical quality measure execution.
Outcome: clinical quality measure computation accuracy

Title: Large Language Model Performance and Clinical Reasoning Tasks
Summary: Assesses how well large language models perform on structured clinical reasoning tasks compared to expected clinician reasoning pathways. Examines strengths and failure modes of LLM-based clinical reasoning.
Outcome: clinical reasoning performance

Title: Leveraging large language models to enhance cytopathology: Opportunities, challenges, and future directions; a practical review from the ASC Clinical Practice Committee
Summary: A practical review from the American Society of Cytopathology examining how LLMs and vision-language models can support structured reporting, diagnostic assistance, quality control, education, and workflow integration in cytopathology. Discusses current opportunities, challenges, and future directions for adoption.
Outcome: structured reporting and diagnostic assistance in cytopathology

Title: General-purpose large language models outperform specialized clinical AI tools on medical benchmarks
Summary: Compares specialized clinical AI tools (OpenEvidence, UpToDate Expert AI) against frontier general-purpose LLMs (GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.6) on MedQA questions, HealthBench items, and real de-identified physician queries. Frontier general-purpose LLMs outperformed the specialized clinical AI tools across all three evaluation stages.
Outcome: medical benchmark / clinical query performance comparison

Title: Clinician Use of a General-Purpose Large Language Model in Hospital Medicine: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study
Summary: A mixed-methods pilot study examining how hospital medicine clinicians actually use a general-purpose LLM in daily practice. Combines usage data with qualitative feedback to characterize adoption patterns, perceived value, and concerns.
Outcome: clinician usage patterns and perceived utility

Title: LLM-as-a-Judge in Healthcare: A Scoping Analysis of Applications, Methods, and Human Alignment
Summary: A scoping analysis of how LLMs are used as automated judges to evaluate other AI outputs or clinical text in healthcare applications. Reviews methods for LLM-as-a-judge and examines how well these automated judgments align with human expert assessment.
Outcome: alignment of LLM-based evaluation with human judgment

Title: Can Large Language Models Identify When an Upper Extremity Problem Needs Nonurgent Attention? An Assessment of Multiple LLM Chatbots
Summary: Presented five LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Copilot, Gemini, and PerplexityChat) with urgent and nonurgent upper-extremity symptom scenarios and assessed whether they correctly identified which needed nonurgent attention. Chatbots identified nonurgent conditions with 97% positive predictive value and 89% negative predictive value, improving to 96% and 97% respectively after follow-up questioning.
Outcome: triage/urgency identification accuracy (97% PPV / 89% NPV)

Title: Large language models provide unsafe answers to patient-posed medical questions
Summary: A physician-led red-teaming study evaluated 888 responses from four chatbots (Claude, Gemini, GPT-4o, Llama3-70B) to 222 patient-posed medical questions spanning internal medicine, women's health, and pediatrics. Problematic response rates ranged from 21.6% (Claude) to 43.2% (Llama), with unsafe responses ranging from 5% (Claude) to 13% (GPT-4o, Llama).
Outcome: answer safety for patient medical questions

Title: AI-driven Medical Care: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Generating Personalized Stroke Education Materials
Summary: Evaluates the ability of large language models to generate personalized patient education materials for stroke care. Assesses quality and appropriateness of the LLM-generated educational content for stroke patients.
Outcome: quality of generated patient education materials

Title: Assessing large language model responses to pediatric depression FAQs: a cross-sectional study on readability, accuracy, and sentiment
Summary: A cross-sectional study assessing LLM-generated responses to frequently asked questions about pediatric depression across readability, factual accuracy, and sentiment. Aims to characterize the quality of LLM output as a patient/parent information source.
Outcome: readability/accuracy/sentiment of generated responses

Title: Arkangel AI, OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Medisearch: Are They Objectively up to Medical Standards? A Real-Life Assessment of LLM Chatbots in Health Care
Summary: Four independent-expert clinical vignettes (orthopedics, pediatrics, gynecology, psychiatry) were answered by four conversational AI agents (Arkangel AI, OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Medisearch) and rated by clinicians on an 8-criterion Likert scale. Overall satisfaction ranged from 71.1% to 93% across agents, with significant variability in bias and patient-safety criteria.
Outcome: clinician-rated satisfaction/quality across correctness/safety/bias criteria

Title: Psychiatric Risk Associated With Large Language Model Chatbots: An Emerging Concern
Summary: Discusses emerging reports of psychiatric harm, including psychosis, depression, and suicide, associated with heavy use of LLM chatbots, often marked by delusions reinforced by the model. Raises concern about the psychiatric safety of widely used conversational AI tools.
Outcome: psychiatric safety risk associated with chatbot use

Title: A roadmap for medical large language models: a review of foundations, applications, and challenges
Summary: A review presenting a roadmap for translating medical large language models into clinical practice, organized around six interconnected challenges: hallucination/factual reliability, evaluation/benchmarks/clinical validity, safety/ethics/privacy/regulation, robustness/generalization, knowledge updating/maintenance, and human oversight/workflow integration. Argues that clinical usefulness cannot be judged by benchmark performance alone.
Outcome: clinical translation and deployment readiness of medical LLMs

Title: Using Large Language Models to Audit Model Healthcare Biases
Summary: Uses a Stanford Healthcare red-teaming dataset of prompts, outputs, and expert bias labels to test how model size and prompting technique affect LLM-based bias detection (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, Llama3.3, o1-mini). Found that the smaller o1-mini outperformed GPT-4o in precision (up to 53% higher) and F1 score (up to 10% higher), and that Thread-of-Thought prompting improved bias detection across models.
Outcome: bias-detection performance (precision/F1)

Title: Large Language Models as Unified Multimodal Learners for Clinical Prediction
Summary: Proposes converting all patient data (free-text and structured) into a single natural-language sequence and fine-tuning a pretrained language model end-to-end for clinical prediction, with no task-specific fusion architecture. Evaluated on in-hospital mortality (MIMIC-III), graft failure prediction, and emergency triage classification, this unified textual approach matched or exceeded task-specific multimodal baselines and outperformed a clinically deployed gradient boosting system on graft failure prediction.
Outcome: mortality prediction, graft failure prediction, triage classification

Title: Characterizing Parental Use of a HIPAA-Compliant Large Language Model Chatbot in Rare Pediatric Diseases: Insights from Think-Aloud Sessions
Summary: Uses think-aloud sessions to characterize how parents of children with rare pediatric diseases use a HIPAA-compliant LLM chatbot to seek information and support. Reports on usability, information needs, and parental experience with the tool.
Outcome: parental usability/experience with chatbot

Title: LLM-assisted systematic review of large language models in clinical medicine
Summary: An LLM-assisted systematic review framework identified 4,609 peer-reviewed studies evaluating LLMs in clinical medicine published between January 2022 and September 2025. Found that most studies used simulated or exam-style scenarios rather than real-world patient data (only 1,048 of studies), with ChatGPT/OpenAI models dominating (65.7% of evaluated models) and patient-facing communication/education the largest application area.
Outcome: landscape and evidence gaps in clinical LLM research

Title: Reasoning in Real World Clinical Care: Why Large Language Models Are Not Yet Safe for Autonomous Clinical Decision Support
Summary: Argues that while LLMs can pass medical licensing exams and rival physicians on curated diagnostic cases, they are not yet safe for autonomous triage of self-presenting, undifferentiated patients with no clinician in the loop. Identifies that current evaluations use complete, well-curated simulations that fail to test reasoning under missing information, and that LLM assistant-like behaviors (credulity, agreeableness, miscalibration) can amplify failure modes.
Outcome: safety assessment of autonomous LLM-based clinical triage/decision support

Title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
Summary: Conducts a systematic sensitivity analysis of general-purpose LLMs (GPT-3.5, Llama3) and medical-specific models (ClinicalBERT, BioLlama3, BioBERT) using the MedMCQA benchmark, testing natural and adversarial prompt perturbations. Found that even minor phrasing changes can alter clinical advice and that targeted adversarial prompts can provoke harmful outputs, showing medical LLMs are not intrinsically robust.
Outcome: robustness/consistency of clinical question-answering under prompt variation

Title: Evaluation of large language model responses to patient questions on oral anticoagulant therapy: a comparative expert assessment
Summary: Compares responses from ChatGPT-4.5, Gemini Pro 2.5, and DeepSeek-V3 to 11 frequently asked patient questions about five oral anticoagulants against expert-derived reference answers. Blinded clinical pharmacists rated all responses on accuracy, clarity, and completeness; ChatGPT-4.5 achieved the highest ratings overall, with warfarin-related queries showing the largest differences between models.
Outcome: quality/accuracy of LLM patient education responses on anticoagulation

Title: Multilingual Evaluation of a Large Language Model-Based Primary Care Chatbot
Summary: Evaluates PCP-Bot, an English-developed GPT-4o-based clinical chatbot that collects patient concerns and generates physician-ready summaries, when used by 31 bilingual participants role-playing patients in English and a second language (Mandarin, Spanish, or Hindi). Assesses whether the chatbot's performance degrades in multilingual clinical settings compared to its native English use.
Outcome: multilingual performance and summary quality of a primary-care chatbot

Title: Large Language Model-Based Behavioral Activation Chatbot for Young People With Depression Using Artificial Users and Clinical Experts: Mixed Methods Evaluation
Summary: Implements a GPT-4o-based chatbot using a structured system prompt to deliver a single-session behavioral activation intervention for people aged 14-29 with depression, generating 48 sessions with AI-simulated artificial users derived from varied clinical vignettes. Independent clinical expert assessment evaluated how well the LLM-based chatbot delivered this structured psychological intervention.
Outcome: feasibility/quality of delivering a structured behavioral therapy intervention

Title: Feasibility of a Large Language Model Chatbot to Support Parental Understanding in the PICU
Summary: Tests a GPT-4o-based, EHR-informed chatbot answering questions from 14 parents of children in the pediatric intensive care unit over 10-minute sessions. Parents showed sustained engagement (median 6 questions/session, 96% positive ratings, NPS +57) and the chatbot's 1,225 generated sentences were 99.3% accurate, with all errors classified as minor, supporting progression to a randomized controlled trial.
Outcome: parental engagement/satisfaction and response accuracy (99.3%)

Title: Research on patient-facing chatbots based on large language models in the care of older people: a living systematic review
Summary: A living systematic review of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library identified 9 studies (from 1,228 records) on patient-facing LLM chatbots in the care of older people, with a median sample size of 12 older participants. Found that most studies used qualitative methods and none reported effectiveness data from a fully operational deployment, indicating the field remains in an early phase.
Outcome: evidence landscape for LLM chatbots in geriatric care
